record.title: OpenAI releases 722 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts across 372 result families with partial Lean formalization
record.summary: On October 6, OpenAI published a GitHub collection of mathematical manuscripts generated by an internal frontier model, alongside some Lean formalizations and process details. The repository README reports 722 manuscripts across 372 families and approximately 4,000 attempted problems. OpenAI says not all results are formalized and some unformalized work may contain errors. An independent mathematics advisory group calls the release an important first step, while saying mathematical assessment and human understanding remain to be done.
organizations: Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI published the “Sharing AI progress in mathematics” release and linked public repository on 2026-10-06.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The repository README reports 722 manuscripts organized into 372 families, covering results at different verification stages.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says approximately 4,000 problems were posed and the average result used compute equivalent to roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking, with stated exceptions.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The README says some outputs build on earlier model results, not all manuscripts have Lean formalizations, and some unformalized results could contain issues.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: AGMAI described the collection as an important event but said only the mathematical community can assess impact; it characterized public release as the beginning, not completion, of human understanding and did not endorse the process.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The number of novel, correct, independently accepted results; their attribution to the model rather than prior work or human contributions; and any downstream research impact are not established by the inspected release materials.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Lean catalogue describes itself as listing papers with a formalized main result; a read-only count of the unpinned main-branch manifest found 162 source entries. This does not establish that the entries build successfully or have been independently audited.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent mathematician assessment or verified error/correction record for individual result families was identified.
Model identity, full prompt and attempt-level data are not uniformly disclosed for the collection.
Novelty relative to prior literature and earlier model-generated results is unresolved across the large collection.

brief.importance_rationale: If a substantial share of the released results are novel and correct, a single frontier-model evaluation has generated a broad body of usable mathematical work and could change research practice. Score 6 reflects potentially major impact across mathematics and AI evaluation while leaving the number of valid novel results and their uptake unverified.
limitations: The 722-manuscript and 372-family counts, attempt count and compute estimate are OpenAI repository or company statements, not independently audited measurements.
The collection includes results at different verification stages; the README explicitly says not all results are formalized and some unformalized results may have issues.
Some manuscripts build on earlier model outputs, and the checked release does not establish theorem-level novelty or exclusive model authorship.
AGMAI’s response is an independent statement about release practice and process, not an audit of the mathematical results.
No peer-reviewed acceptance, independent proof verification, broad model access, complete attempt-level record or measured downstream use was established in this pass.

The 162 manifest entries are a count of catalog records, not independently verified successful builds or accepted theorems. The current main branch was not pinned to a commit, and the catalog count is not directly comparable to 722 manuscripts because families may contain multiple papers.
organizations: Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence

The repository README reports 722 manuscripts across 372 families and approximately 4,000 attempted problems. OpenAI says not all results are formalized and some unformalized work may contain errors. technical.claimed_result: OpenAI says the collection contains new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model, after approximately 4,000 attempted problems; it estimates the average result used compute equivalent to roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking.
technical.compute_or_cost: Publisher estimates about three hours of ChatGPT Pro-equivalent compute per average result, with exceptions; this is not an independently audited compute or dollar-cost measurement.
technical.demonstrated_result: OpenAI published a public repository containing manuscripts, supporting files and some formal proof artifacts. The repository README states that the collection has 722 manuscripts organized into 372 families.
technical.implementation_status: Public GitHub repository released; model remains internal according to the release post.
technical.mechanism: An internal OpenAI model was prompted on open mathematical problems; OpenAI aggregates outputs into result families and manuscripts and releases some Lean proof formalizations, reasoning summaries and process statistics.
technical.novelty: The release is a new large-scale public collection and workflow disclosure. Individual mathematical novelty and attribution remain for specialist review.
technical.regime: One lab-reported release produced with an unreleased internal model; results vary in verification stage, and not all have Lean formalizations.
technical.reproducibility: The repository includes manuscript-specific materials and formalizations for some results. Its Lean README describes one large library, recommends compiling small portions at a time and directs users to separate Comparator instructions. The formalization catalogue contained 162 source entries in the inspected unpinned main-branch file; no Lean build, Comparator run or independent theorem audit was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: No independent theorem-by-theorem verification or novelty assessment was identified in this targeted release check; the comparison baseline is therefore not established.

brief.title: OpenAI releases 722 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts across 372 result families with partial Lean formalization
brief.why_it_matters: The release creates a large, inspectable corpus for evaluating frontier-model mathematical work and its verification pipeline. Its impact depends on theorem-level novelty, correctness and human assimilation, none of which can be inferred from the manuscript count or the lab announcement.

related.summary: This is a distinct Oct 26 research announcement with new claimed results and expert-led review arrangements, following OpenAI's separate Oct 6 mathematics collection release. The earlier collection does not establish these new theorem claims.

other.title: OpenAI releases AI-generated mathematical research claims with specialist-led review groups
other.summary: On October 26, 2026, OpenAI announced three AI-generated research claims spanning harmonic analysis, computational complexity and quantum field theory, and described external expert-led groups to examine them. OpenAI says it publicly released manuscripts and Lean formalizations for local smoothing and an ETH refutation; a separate physics claim remains without public AI-produced artifacts. The official formalization catalog maps local-smoothing declarations to a Lean source file whose proof bodies invoke existing development theorems, and maps the ETH exact-counting theorem to a separate source file with a completed proof body. The linked ComparatorChallenges files contain `sorry` placeholders, but the repository instructions identify them as challenge configurations, so those placeholders alone do not refute formal proof coverage. This activation did not pin the repository revision, run Lean, audit dependencies or axioms, establish complete manuscript-to-formal correspondence, or obtain independent mathematical review. The theorem results therefore remain source-attributed claims with correctness, novelty and community acceptance unresolved.

related.summary: This specific Oct 6 manuscript is included in OpenAI’s broader mathematics collection release; the collection event does not replace the distinct theorem-level research identity.

other.title: OpenAI paper encodes Turing-machine halting in forced Navier–Stokes particle motion
other.summary: An OpenAI-authored paper constructs a smooth external force that encodes any finite Turing machine and input into a Navier–Stokes flow: from zero initial velocity, one fixed particle enters a fixed open region exactly if the machine halts. The core construction uses fixed positive computable viscosity, compact spatial support and bounded kinetic energy. These are source-reported mathematical results, not independently reviewed here. The construction is forced and remains globally smooth; it does not show unforced blowup or resolve the Clay Millennium problem.
